prompt_en: An intimate photograph creates a coherent complex photographic scene with a woman whose visible face and hair follow the supplied reference image, absorbed in one connected moment of everyday activity: restoring the lifted ribbon on the same hat at the existing seated work surface. Use the reference for facial contours, dark eyes, natural pink lips and the dark chin-length bob with wispy fringe. Her calm, attentive presence and natural skin texture carry the portrait; a slight lean toward the work gives her face and hands a shared depth plane. The photographer is close to the work surface, in a gently elevated front three-quarter view, framing the face, both shoulder-to-forearm chains, both complete hands, the hat and the turned jacket cuff in one intimate horizontal photograph. The woman holds the sewing needle between her right thumb and index finger while her left fingertips pin the ribbon to the hat beside the fresh stitch. The sewing needle has one metallic shaft, a pointed tip and a clearly exposed eye threaded with golden thread. At this shutter moment the needle has emerged from the ribbon: her right fingers grip the middle of its shaft, leaving the point, the shaft toward the eye and the open eye exposed in the air. One continuous length of golden thread passes through that eye and runs in a simple unobstructed curve to the fresh stitch in the exposed ribbon immediately beside her left pinning fingertips. The lifted loose portion of the ribbon and the short newly secured portion belong to that same hat, so the small repair and its useful result can be read together. The fingers touch the needle itself, with the thin thread visibly separate from the metallic shaft. The turned jacket cuff next to the working hands faces the camera across a broad area. Fine interlaced yarns remain visible across the same textile surface beside its stitched edge. The small over-and-under crossings of the fine yarns sit directly beside the continuous row of sewing stitches following that cuff edge; the cuff's weave and its seam occupy the same exposed patch. Her bent elbows keep the hands close together over the supported hat, and her seated torso rests comfortably behind the surface. The nearer cuff, acting grip, needle eye, thread route and ribbon contact are spread within one clear plane with separate visible contours. The chair back and edge of the work surface retain enough form to identify the seated repair setting behind her. Side window light grazes the cuff and the silver needle, separating the yarn crossings and stitch row with small natural shadows. The hat remains supported at the lower frame, the face occupies the upper side, and the joined hands form the quiet visual center between them. Moderate depth of field keeps the eyes, complete acting hands, needle and cuff weave crisp together, while the existing place cue remains softly identifiable. Render the moment with restrained documentary intimacy, believable proportions, continuous fingers and wrists, realistic thread thickness, and the tactile clarity of an actual close photograph. A shared focus zone draws the recognizable face, the needle-gripping hand with its ribbon contact, and a softly legible chair and work-surface edge into one continuous reading.
